correctness.rationale: Every affine minorant \(h(x)=cx+d\) of \(a x^2/2\) satisfies \(d\le-c^2/(2a)\); raising the intercept to equality can only increase descent distance, reducing the optimization to tangent minorants. For \(0<\Delta<G\), the exact difference identity \(d_{y_\star}-d_y=(y-y_\star)^2/(2y)\) proves the unique global maximizing slope. The cases \(\Delta=G\) and \(\Delta>G\) are handled separately, yielding nonattainment and infinite slowness respectively. Substitution into the W inequality gives the stated necessary-and-sufficient trial-modulus thresholds. The packaged exact-rational checker independently replays these identities on multiple rational parameter families.

residual_risks: The affine-minorant calculation is elementary once descent-slowness is defined, so an equivalent scalar envelope may exist in older bundle/error-bound literature under different terminology.

The one-dimensional unconstrained frontier need not survive unchanged under constraints or anisotropic multidimensional curvature.

value.rationale: The affine W-certificate is the load-bearing new mechanism of the recent parameter-free method, and the trial modulus \(\mu\) is explicitly intended to be searched adaptively. The scalar quadratic is the canonical exact quadratic-growth model, so a complete existence frontier is a natural calibration rather than an arbitrary slice. The formula quantifies precisely how much the trial modulus must be inflated when the target gap is too ambitious, and the nonattained \(r=1\) boundary shows a subtle limitation not visible from the source one-way gap theorem. This gives concrete guidance for interpreting certificate success/failure and separates geometric attainability from the logical validity of the gap bound.
